Electronic countermeasures are not wide-band jammers. They are designed to spoof and confuse radar systems belonging to your opponents. There is a wide range of methods to modify various facets of the RF signal you transmit to fool the receiving radar system. ECM works by returning those "twisted" signals back to the receiver with a much larger amplitude than their reflected signal.

Systems integration means you recognize your own systems and do not "attack" them with your ECM. A very good case is that of the Iraqi Air Force's Mirage fighters during Gulf I. Iraq flew France's export version of the Mirage, which had different electronic systems than the French use in their national version. That is why Iraq's Mirages were ineffective against the French. They were blind as far as French AF fighters were concerned. The French ECM easily defeated the Iraqi's radar and the Iraqi ECM was almost blind to the French AF systems.

ECM is not transmitted blindly into the air. It needs something on which to base its transmissions, that being the incoming radar signal from your opponent. Radars operate on many frequencies and have different characteristics that depend on the type of broadcast: (Searching, tracking) and type of radar (directional, height finding). Each type of radar can be attacked by a wide variety methods to either hide you, make dozens/hundreds of you, slide your true position away from where you are, etc.

And then there are the many, many, anti-radiation missile systems fielded by various NATO countries.
